clue.text: Knowing about one manuscript from this copy

indicators.note: about means going round, so the word for knowing wraps the other pieces

parts.note: fly is slang for knowing or sharp-witted
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A clever scholar copying a manuscript from an existing copy.
explanation.walkthrough: A flimsy is thin paper, and by extension a carbon copy made on it; 'from this' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A flimsy was the thin carbon duplicate typed alongside a top sheet, so a copy.

clue.text: One of these old angles on the line

definitions.text: One of these old angles on the line

parts.words: One of these old angles on the line
parts.note: angle is an old word for the barbed device tied on an angler's line, not a geometrical angle

explanation.definitionFit: The barbed hooks used to catch fish were once called angles, hence anglers.

clue.text: Nice tax but somehow not quite right

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters are put together in some other way

explanation.surface: A pleasant tax that still feels a bit off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imprecise is approximately but not exactly correct.

clue.text: Food for beach charmers, some might say

indicators.note: says the phrase is spoken, so it is what it sounds like that counts

parts.note: enchantresses on the shore would be witches of the sand

explanation.surface: Lunch for those who charm at the seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: Slices of bread with a filling are a common packed food.

clue.text: One with an eye for beauty

definitions.text: One with an eye for beauty

parts.words: One with an eye for beauty
parts.note: the proverb says beauty lies in the eye of a particular person, the one doing the looking, rather than in the thing seen

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'beauty is in the eye of the ...' names the onlooker whose eye decides what is beautiful.

clue.text: Depth limit, upper section, for what 4 sees

definitions.text: Depth limit, upper section, for what 4 sees

parts.words: Depth limit, upper section, for what 4 sees
parts.note: beauty is only skin deep, so what the onlooker of 4 across sees stops at the top layer of skin

explanation.definitionFit: The outer layer of the skin, the limit of depth for beauty in the saying 'beauty is only skin deep'.

clue.text: Stone in layers lower around New York

indicators.note: around means the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: a lower is something that lows or moos, an ox

explanation.surface: Rock strata lying lower beneath New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded variety of chalcedony, its colours lying in parallel layers.

clue.text: Interlude, without hesitation, ruined the neatness

definitions.text: Interlude, without hesitation, ruined the neatness

indicators.note: ruined says the remaining letters are wrecked into a new order
without means the hesitation is taken away from the word

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: An interval that came in at once spoiled the tidiness.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ER from INTERLUDE leaves INTLUDE, which 'ruined' rearranges. The whole clue also defines: a diluent ruins a drink's neatness.
explanation.definitionFit: A diluting agent such as water spoils a neat spirit by watering it down.

clue.text: Heeds sunken ships, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is as spoken, not as written

parts.note: sunken ships are wrecks

explanation.surface: Notices ships that have gone down.
explanation.definitionFit: To reck is an old verb for to care about or pay attention to.

clue.text: Mischief-maker one finds among the Zulus

definitions.note: the definition describes something one finds among Zulus, a regiment

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous sprite
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A troublemaker turns up in a Zulu village.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the Zulu word for an armed band of warriors.

clue.text: Problem about a bird's bone

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the word for problem goes round the bird

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem
a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Puzzling over an issue with a bird's bone.
explanation.definitionFit: The breastbone, to which the ribs attach, is a bone of the chest.

clue.text: In pencil Lydia retraced writing so pleasing

indicators.note: retraced means the run is traced back, so it is read from right to left
In tells us the letters sit inside the words pencil Lydia

explanation.surface: Lydia's pencil writing, gone over again, looks delightful.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside 'pencil Lydia' sits CILLYDI; 'retraced' reads it backwards. 'writing' is link, nodding to the idyll as a kind of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a charming pastoral scene, so the adjective means charmingly pleasant.

clue.text: Service chief sets out the war idea

indicators.note: sets out suggests laying the letters out afresh in a new order

explanation.surface: An officer in the forces lays out the idea of going to war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' suggests the armed forces, but it is restaurant service.
explanation.definitionFit: The man in charge of the waiting staff in a restaurant runs its table service.

clue.text: Helen's godfather

parts.note: Helen of Troy was the daughter of a god, so her father was literally a god-father, not a baptismal sponsor

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the king of the Olympians fathered Helen of Troy on Leda, so he is both god and father.

clue.text: The mood for pointing out .

definitions.meaning: the grammatical mood of plain statements
serving to show or signal something

explanation.definitionFit: The grammatical mood for simple statements, and an adjective meaning that which points something out.

clue.text: Is 4's vision of beauty such an illusion ?

definitions.text: Is 4's vision of beauty such an illusion ?

parts.words: Is 4's vision of beauty such an illusion
parts.note: asks whether what the onlooker of 4 across sees as beauty is a trick of the eye, naming the kind of illusion

explanation.definitionFit: A trick of the eye is called a visual illusion, the adjective relating to sight.

clue.text: where in London to get gin additive at'the innkeeper's expense ?

parts.note: lime juice is added to gin in a gimlet
a drink on the house is paid for by the innkeeper

explanation.surface: A London spot for free gin with a twist.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 14 down's dots. 'At the innkeeper's expense' is on the house, so the lime sits on the house. LIMEHOUSE is a district of East London.
explanation.definitionFit: Limehouse is a riverside district in the East End of London.

clue.text: Form of 10 in Ireland

indicators.note: a form of something is a rearranged shape of it, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: 10 refers to the answer of 10 across, the breastbone

explanation.surface: A shape of something found in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of the 10 across answer are rearranged to make the name of an Irish province.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the four historic provinces of Ireland, in the south-west.

clue.text: Put fresh order into the back row

parts.note: the rear is the back
a range is a row, as of mountains or houses

explanation.surface: Reshuffling the seating in the back row.
explanation.definitionFit: To set things out again in a new sequence.

clue.text: Shaft unlikely to be seen deep in a mine

definitions.text: Shaft unlikely to be seen deep in a mine

parts.words: Shaft unlikely to be seen deep in a mine
parts.note: a mine has shafts, but this shaft is a ray of daylight, which never reaches underground

explanation.definitionFit: A shaft of light from the sun cannot penetrate deep underground workings.

clue.text: Battledress is not the gear for him

definitions.text: Battledress is not the gear for him

parts.words: Battledress is not the gear for him
parts.note: someone taking no side wears no uniform, and the gear also hints at the car gear with no drive engaged

explanation.definitionFit: A non-combatant takes no side in a war, and the same word names a car's disengaged gear.

clue.text: Praise a variety of meadow-sweet

indicators.note: a variety is a different version, so the letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Admiring a kind of wild flower in a meadow.
explanation.definitionFit: Meadowsweet is a flowering plant once classed in this genus of shrubs and herbs.

clue.text: A building site up in a street in Guildford

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: a street gives A plus ST, the abbreviation for street

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the piece is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a lot is a plot of land for building

explanation.surface: A building plot found up a street in a Surrey town.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' means read from the bottom. Astolat is the Arthurian home of Elaine, which Malory identified with Guildford, the county town of Surrey.
explanation.definitionFit: Malory's Morte d'Arthur names the Arthurian town of Elaine as the place now called Guildford.

clue.text: Old street for food

definitions.meaning: a London street of hack writers, renamed in the nineteenth century

explanation.definitionFit: Grub Street was the old London home of hack writers, and grub is also slang for something to eat.

clue.text: How they stared when Jock went without a penny!

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the Scots word goes round the coin

parts.note: gaed is the Scots past tense of go, and Jock is the crossword's Scotsman
P is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Onlookers were open-mouthed when a Scot left without a penny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but here means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare open-mouthed in wonder is to gape, here in the past tense.

clue.text: Feature a Michaelmas daisy from the east

definitions.text: Feature a Michaelmas daisy from the east

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
the Michaelmas daisy is a kind of aster

explanation.surface: Describing a flower that comes from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a plant like a Michaelmas daisy that comes from the Far East.
explanation.definitionFit: This annual garden flower, related to the asters, was brought to the West from East Asia.

clue.text: Churchill followed some chicken with some

definitions.text: Churchill followed some chicken with some

parts.words: Churchill followed some chicken with some
parts.note: Churchill told the Canadian parliament that Britain would have its ... wrung like a chicken's, then quipped 'Some chicken! Some ...!'

explanation.definitionFit: Churchill's 1941 retort 'Some chicken! Some ...!' named the part of the bird that would be wrung.

clue.text: Still one Himalayan mystery

parts.note: yet means still, as in not yet gone
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Another unsolved puzzle in the mountains of Asia.
explanation.definitionFit: The Abominable Snowman is a legendary creature said to roam the Himalayas.

clue.text: Wealthy newcomer's standard not quite county (legally)

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

indicators.note: not quite means the word falls just short, losing its final letter

parts.note: in law the venue is the county in which a trial is held

explanation.surface: Someone newly rich falls short of county society's standard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'County' in Britain also means the landed gentry, which sharpens the snobbish surface.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart who has recently gained wealth but not social acceptance.

clue.text: Byronic castle giving its prisoner the shivers ?

definitions.text: Byronic castle giving its prisoner the shivers ?

parts.words: Byronic castle giving its prisoner the shivers
parts.note: Byron wrote of the prisoner of a lakeside Swiss castle; split, its name reads as a chill being put on

explanation.definitionFit: Byron's poem 'The Prisoner of ...' is set in a castle on Lake Geneva.

clue.text: Played by Coleridge's visionary damsel

parts.note: in Kubla Khan Coleridge describes a vision of an Abyssinian maid playing an instrument

explanation.definitionFit: Kubla Khan: 'A damsel with a ... In a vision once I saw', a stringed instrument struck with hammers.

clue.text: Pretty messy container of 1dn's catch

parts.note: the idiom a pretty ... of fish means a muddle, and fish are what hooks on a line catch

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'a pretty ... of fish' means an awkward mess, the vessel holding the fish.
